slots.practicalActivity: Install Git on your own machine (Windows/macOS/Linux), confirm it with git --version, then run git config --global user.name and git config --global user.email with your real name and email so every future commit is correctly attributed.
slots.deliverable: Terminal output from git --version and git config --global --list showing your real name and email set.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a real practice project folder, run git init, create and edit at least two files across separate rounds of git add and git commit -m with specific, meaningful messages (not 'fix' or 'update'), then review the result with git status and git log.
slots.deliverable: A local Git repository whose git log shows at least 3 real commits with specific, meaningful messages.

slots.practicalActivity: In your practice repository, create a branch with git switch -c feature-login, make a commit on it, switch back to main with git switch main, and confirm main's content is untouched; list all branches with git branch and delete a throwaway one with git branch -d.
slots.deliverable: A repository with at least one real feature branch containing a commit that main does not have, confirmed via git log on each branch.

slots.practicalActivity: Create two diverging branches from main that each edit the exact same line of the same file; merge one with git merge to produce a real merge commit, then on a separate pair of branches use git rebase to produce a clean linear history instead; on the merge pair, deliberately trigger the conflict, read the <<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>> markers, edit the file to the correct final content, and finish with git add and git commit.
slots.deliverable: A repository containing one real merge commit (two parents), one rebased branch with a linear history and no merge commit, and one resolved merge conflict visible in git log -p.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter review for Git Fundamentals: without looking back at the lessons, create a brand-new branch in your practice repository, deliberately conflict it with main on a real line of code, resolve the conflict correctly, then rebase a second, unrelated feature branch cleanly onto main.
slots.deliverable: A short note confirming you performed init/add/commit, branch creation, a real merge conflict resolution, and a clean rebase again from memory, with the resulting commit hashes.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a new repository on GitHub, connect your local practice repository to it with git remote add origin <url>, push with git push -u origin main, then make a small change directly on GitHub's web editor and practice git fetch origin followed by git log main..origin/main before running git pull origin main to bring it in.
slots.deliverable: A real GitHub repository containing your pushed commits, plus terminal output from git remote -v confirming origin is correctly configured.

slots.practicalActivity: Push a real feature branch with at least one commit, open a pull request against main with a clear title and a description explaining what changed and why, then walk through its Conversation, Commits, Checks, and Files changed tabs.
slots.deliverable: A real, open pull request URL on your GitHub repository with a written title and description.

slots.practicalActivity: On your open pull request's Files changed tab, hover a specific line and leave a real inline comment attached to it, mark at least one file Viewed, then submit a review using one of the three verdicts (Comment, Approve, or Request changes) with specific, actionable wording.
slots.deliverable: A submitted pull request review containing at least one line-anchored inline comment and a chosen verdict.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a specific, well-written GitHub Issue on your repository (what you expected vs. what happened, or what problem a feature solves), add it to a new Project board, then open or edit a pull request so its description includes 'Closes #<issue-number>'.
slots.deliverable: A real GitHub Issue tracked on a Project board, referenced by 'Closes #N' in a pull request description.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter review for GitHub Essentials: on your practice repository, walk end-to-end through push, pull request, review, and issue-linking one more time without referring back to the lessons, and write out from memory what each of a pull request's four tabs is for.
slots.deliverable: A short written explanation of the Conversation, Commits, Checks, and Files changed tabs, checked against a real pull request you opened yourself.

slots.practicalActivity: In one practice repository, simulate Git Flow end to end: create develop, branch feature/* off it and merge back, then cut release/* and merge it into both main and develop with a tag; in a second practice repository, simulate trunk-based development by creating and merging three small, short-lived branches straight into main in one sitting.
slots.deliverable: Two practice repositories — one demonstrating a full Git Flow cycle, one demonstrating three trunk-based merges — plus a one-paragraph recommendation of which strategy fits a named real project type and why.

slots.practicalActivity: Fork a small real public repository on GitHub into your own account, clone your fork locally, create a branch with a small real change, push it to your fork, open a pull request comparing across forks back to the original repository, then add the original as an upstream remote and run git fetch upstream to confirm it resolves.
slots.deliverable: A real cross-fork pull request URL, plus git remote -v output showing both origin (your fork) and upstream (the original repository).

slots.practicalActivity: In a repository with real history (yours or a cloned open-source project), run git blame on a file you didn't write, pick a line whose reasoning surprises you, and run git show on its commit hash to read the full message; separately, in your own practice repository create an annotated tag (git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "..."), push it explicitly, and draft a GitHub Release from it using 'Generate release notes'.
slots.deliverable: A written trace of one unfamiliar line back to its commit, author, and reasoning via blame+show, plus a real GitHub Release built from a pushed annotated tag.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a new repository and add a .gitignore from GitHub's own template library for a language you know, before your first commit; then deliberately force-add a file matching one of its patterns, practice git rm --cached to stop tracking it, and set up a global ignore file (git config --global core.excludesfile) for your own editor/OS noise.
slots.deliverable: A repository with a pre-first-commit .gitignore, a demonstrated git rm --cached recovery, and a configured global ~/.gitignore_global on your own machine.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter review for Collaborative Workflows: write one paragraph stating which branching strategy your upcoming Chapter 5 capstone will use and why, confirm your forked pull request, annotated tag, and Release from this chapter are all still live on GitHub, and explain from memory why .gitignore can't undo an already-committed secret.
slots.deliverable: A written branching-strategy decision for your capstone project, plus confirmation that your fork, pull request, tag, and Release from this chapter still exist.

slots.practicalActivity: In a real repository, add a minimal workflow file at .github/workflows/explore.yml triggered on push, with at least two echo steps and a uses: actions/checkout@v4 step; push it, find the resulting run on the Actions tab, then click into the job and read the expanded step logs in order.
slots.deliverable: A real GitHub Actions workflow run with its expanded, step-by-step logs visible on your repository's Actions tab.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a real test-running workflow to your repository, triggered on both push to main and pull requests targeting main; open a pull request with a deliberately failing test and confirm the red X appears on both the commit and the PR's Checks tab, then confirm you can still merge it despite the failure since no branch protection rule exists yet.
slots.deliverable: A pull request showing a failed status check on both the commit list and the Checks tab, with a written note confirming the merge button was not blocked by default.

slots.practicalActivity: Extend your test workflow with a second job gated by if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main', using needs: to depend on the test job; add a fake deploy step (an echo is fine) that reads a real repository secret, then open a PR and confirm the deploy job does not run, and merge it and confirm the deploy job does run with the secret masked in the logs.
slots.deliverable: A workflow run history showing the deploy job skipped on an open pull request and correctly firing after a real merge to main, with the repository secret masked in the run's logs.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for CI/CD Basics: pick a real project (yours, or an open-source one you use) and determine from its .github/workflows/ folder whether it practices Continuous Integration, Continuous Delivery, or Continuous Deployment, then write two sentences on which of Delivery or Deployment you'd choose for your own capstone and why.
slots.deliverable: A short written classification of a real project's CI/CD stage, plus your own capstone's planned stage and reasoning.

lessons.title: Capstone: A Project With a Real GitHub Workflow

slots.practicalActivity: Build the full capstone repository against the lesson's brief using a real (or realistic practice) code project: meaningful commit history, a feature branch merged via a reviewed pull request with at least one inline comment addressed by a follow-up commit, a deliberate and actually-resolved merge conflict, a written branching-strategy note with an annotated release tag, a .gitignore matching the project from day one, and a .github/workflows/ CI job that runs on every push/PR plus a separate deploy job gated to real merges on main only.
slots.deliverable: One complete GitHub repository satisfying every section of the capstone brief: real history and a resolved conflict, a reviewed pull request, a branching note with an annotated tag, a working .gitignore, and a gated CI/CD workflow.

slots.practicalActivity: Practice walking a stranger through your own capstone repository, out loud, in under five minutes, in the order commit graph -> pull request -> resolved conflict -> Actions tab -> release tag; then write out your own specific answers to the four interview questions from the lesson, tied to your actual workflow file.
slots.deliverable: A written five-minute repository walkthrough script, plus specific written answers to all four capstone interview questions, both tied to your own real repository.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can manage a real Git history through branches, merges, and rebases; collaborate on GitHub with pull requests, code review, forks, issues, and tagged releases; and ship changes through a working GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline that tests every change and deploys only on a real merge to main.
